 The 51-year-old was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault in the UK on Thursday
 By
 Christina Dugan Ramirez Fox News 
 Published
 November 9, 2026 9:29am EST
 | 
 Updated

 close Video WATCH LIVE: Police hold briefing following Russell Brand’s 10-year, 6-month prison sentence for rape, sexual assault 
 Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years, 6 months in a British prison for rape and sexual assault.
 NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!
 Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault. 
 On Monday, Judge Bennathan said that while he would follow the sentencing guidelines, he said Brand "committed sexual offenses against a number of women" and reducing the sentences "would not do justice to the overall gravity" of Brand's criminality.
 Last week, Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault in the U.K. He denied the charges and was acquitted of two additional rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault.
 November 9, 2026, London, UK: Court artist drawing by Elizabeth Cook of Russell Brand in the dock at Southwark Crown Court, London.  (Elizabeth Cook/PA Wire via Zuma Press) 
 He was immediately taken into custody following the verdict, according to the BBC . 
 Brand, 51, was accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009. 
 RUSSELL BRAND FOUND GUILTY OF ONE COUNT OF RAPE AND THREE COUNTS OF SEXUAL ASSAULT 
 Russell Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault in the U.K. (Mike Marsland/WireImage) 
 One woman he was convicted of sexually assaulting gave an impact statement during Monday's proceedings, while three others submitted written statements to the prosecutor.
 "For many years as his star was rising it was impossible to escape seeing him all over the media, being celebrated for his disgusting behavior against women like it was all a joke," she said. "There were many times I felt visibly sick at the sight of him parading around thinking he can get away with anything."
 The woman spoke out of view of the courtroom to preserve her identity.
 Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones read statements by the other three women. Brand was convicted of sexually assaulting the first woman at a London radio station in 2005.
 "Since the sexual assault ... Russell Brand has managed to move on and even forget," she wrote. "Over the years, hearing his voice on television, on social media or seeing his image made me jump."
 According to Sky News , Brand acknowledged that he had been "reckless" and used his fame to pursue sexual relationships, but insisted that the encounters were consensual. He also told the jury that consent was "fundamental, essential and necessary."
 Brand has denied forcing any of the women to engage in sexual activity against their will.
 LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS 
 Brand has previously denied all allegations. (Getty Images) 
 Prosecutors alleged that Brand committed the offenses against six women over a 10-year period. The women testified in court about alleged encounters at a hotel, a bar, a radio station, a workplace and Brand’s home.
 According to a Metropolitan Police press release, detectives began investigating Brand after allegations were made public by U.K. media outlets Channel 4 and The Sunday Times in September 2023.
 GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE 
 The outlets launched a joint investigation into the allegations, resulting in a lengthy article on the Times' website, as well as an episode of Channel 4's documentary series, "Dispatches," called "Russell Brand: In Plain Sight." Both contained a number of anonymous complaints, with women accusing Brand of physical and emotional abuse and bullying, as well as some instances of sexual assault.
 PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE 
 This is a court artist sketch by Elizabeth Cook of Russell Brand in the dock at Southwark Crown Court, in London, Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. (Elizabeth Cook/PA via AP) 
 Police video released Thursday, Nov. 5 and obtained by Fox News Digital shows Brand defending his sexual history during questioning by London's Metropolitan Police.
 During a December 2023 interview, Brand sat alongside his attorney and read a lengthy prepared statement to detectives, insisting that his past sexual encounters were consensual.
 "As I’ve repeatedly stated publicly … I led a very promiscuous life in the past, which I’ve spent years openly denouncing. I’ve never engaged in nonconsensual sexual activity," Brand said.
 Brand also criticized a September 2023 media investigation that brought allegations against him into the public spotlight.
 He described the reporting as "defamatory and fictitious," suggesting that consensual encounters had been "invented or reimagined" as sexual misconduct.
 WATCH: RUSSELL BRAND POLICE INTERVIEW FOOTAGE RELEASED AFTER RAPE CONVICTION 
 Video In a video posted to X last year, Brand thanked his fans for messages of support, then criticized the British government and legal system before addressing the charges directly.
 Russell Brand's wife, Laura Brand, took the stand in the actor's rape and sexual assault trial. (Getty Images) 
 He said that he "was a fool before I lived in the light of the Lord. I was a drug addict, a sex addict and an imbecile, but what I never was was a rapist. I've never engaged in nonconsensual activity. I pray that you can see that by looking in my eyes."

 Brand added, "Of course, I'm now going to have the opportunity to defend these charges in court, and I'm incredibly grateful for that."
 Fox News Digital's Janelle Ash and Stephanie Giang-Paunon contributed to this report. 
 Christina Dugan Ramirez is an entertainment journalist with more than 15 years of experience, including a decade at PEOPLE writing high-profile cover stories, covering Hollywood's biggest events, and interviewing many of the industry's most influential stars before joining Fox News Digital in 2024.
